info.text:
A $5,000 ask can add up to about $238,000 in pay.

Example: a $65,000 start vs. $60,000, both with 3% raises for 30 years. The yearly gap grows from $5,000 to $11,783, and the total gap is $237,877 before taxes.
Put 10% of each year's gap in a 401(k) (half employer match) at an assumed 6% a year: about $55,270 extra after 30 years.
In a 2023 Pew survey, 32% of men and 28% of women asked for more pay when last hired; 66% of those who asked got more than the first offer.

Sources: Pew Research Center (April 2023); example math by FinancePros TV with stated assumptions.
News and education, not financial advice.
